newsitem.title: FRANCE: Grain traders bid again for EU wheat, no details.
newsitem.headline: Grain traders bid again for EU wheat, no details.

text.p: Grain traders have been bidding again today for wheat from the European Union, stepping up a war of nerves with the European Commission over the pace of exports, grain industry sources said.
The volume of bids for licences, which carry an export tax of three Ecus per tonne, was not yet available but would be released by the end of the day, they said.
The French authority which handles most bids had no comment.

Traders are bidding through a stand-by daily system for licences, despite efforts by the European Commisison to limit the amount committed for export between tenders which normally control exports. The next tender is on August 14.
The European Commission rejected daily bids for over a million tonnes of wheat licences on Tuesday and raised the export tax on soft wheat to three Ecus from 0.5 Ecus per tonne.
But within hours of that decision traders were sending in new bids for at least 277,500 tonnes at the new tax level. Wednesday's bidding was set to push the volume higher still.
As Wednesday's bids went in, the Commission issued a new warning that any attempts to secure excessive volumes would prompt it to throw out all pending applications once again.
A Commission spokesman did not however say what an acceptable volume might be.
The Commission has a maximum of three working days to decide whether to use its veto against each bid in the daily channel.

The EU has a large crop for disposal this year but is not yet certain how much of it will be of best quality. Moreover, it is not traditionally willing to allow traders to build up large forward positions in licences before they have matching sales.
Traders argue taking such positions is part of the normal course of business and say a rising dollar is helping to make EU wheat attractive even with a tax.
The licences would allow them to lock in a fixed export tax of three Ecus a tonne until the end of December at the latest.
The dollar hit fresh eight-year highs above 6.38 French francs on Wednesday before steadying around 6.3750 francs.
